record.original_question: Can one use Riemann-Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic results obtained by Venakides, Deift, and Oba for the Toda shock problem, where the driven lattice settles into a one-gap periodic state for sufficiently strong driving?

evidence.quote: The proof of this result, however, was not fully rigorous. There are two open problems here. The first is to use Riemann-Hilbert/steepest-descent methods to prove the results in Venakides et al. rigorously.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the doubly infinite Toda lattice
\[
\dot a_n(t) = a_n(t)\bigl(b_{n+1}(t)-b_n(t)\bigr),\qquad \dot b_n(t)=2\bigl(a_n(t)^2-a_{n-1}(t)^2\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,\ t\ge 0,
\]
with step-like initial data
\[
(a_n(0),b_n(0))\to(\tfrac12,c_\pm)\quad\text{as }n\to\pm\infty,
\]
where the asymptotic constant satisfies $c_- > c_+$ (the "shock" condition; equivalently the left background spectrum lies strictly above the right background spectrum, $\inf\sigma(H_-)>\sup\sigma(H_+)$, when the driving is sufficiently strong so that the two background spectra do not overlap).

It has been shown formally that, in the wedge of space-time variables corresponding to the bulk of the shock, the solution $(a_n(t),b_n(t))$ is asymptotically described, as $t\to\infty$ with $n/t$ in a fixed compact subinterval, by a one-gap (genus-one, elliptic) quasi-periodic finite-gap solution of the Toda lattice expressed in terms of Riemann theta functions associated with a hyperelliptic curve determined by the two backgrounds.

Problem. Using the inverse scattering transform reformulation as a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem on the spectral plane and the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest-descent method (including the construction of appropriate $g$-functions, lens openings, and local parametrices), give a fully rigorous proof, with explicit error estimates, that in the modulation/elliptic region the Toda shock solution converges to the conjectured modulated one-gap finite-gap solution.
artifact.status_search_result: A series of works by Egorova, Michor, and Teschl (notably "Long-time asymptotics for Toda shock waves in the modulation region" arXiv:2001.05184, and the companion paper "Toda shock waves: justification of asymptotics", 2020, plus arXiv:2012.12371 on discrete spectrum/resonances) carries out the Riemann–Hilbert / nonlinear steepest-descent analysis with local parametrices and small-norm arguments, providing a rigorous justification of the Venakides–Deift–Oba asymptotics for the Toda shock problem with non-overlapping background spectra.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for Toda shock waves in the modulation region
status_evidence.snippet: Toda shock waves are asymptotically close to a modulated finite gap solution... main contribution is the solution of local parametrix Riemann–Hilbert problems and rigorous justification.
status_evidence.claim: Provides rigorous RH/steepest-descent justification of the modulation-region asymptotics for the Toda shock problem.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for the Toda shock problem: non-overlapping spectra
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorously derives the long-time asymptotics of the Toda shock wave; verifies the conjecture from Venakides, Deift, and Oba (1991).
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous derivation of Toda shock asymptotics, confirming the Venakides–Deift–Oba results.

status_evidence.title: How Discrete Spectrum and Resonances Influence the Asymptotics of the Toda Shock Wave
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the influence of resonances and eigenvalues on the asymptotics in the elliptic zone.
status_evidence.claim: Extends the rigorous RH analysis to include discrete spectrum effects.
